synthesis_top_issues.title: What happens after a fail is undecided, and saving the remaining time at checkpoints produces unwinnable saves
synthesis_top_issues.problem: The document leaves the retry model open (“checkpoint retry or restart ... still to be decided”) while proposing to “save remaining time at checkpoints”. A player who reaches a checkpoint low on time reloads into a guaranteed fail. That breaks Gate 2's “no dead-end save” rule and the invariant that the outcome “resolves exactly once”. Checkpoints are also scheduled for Gate 3, even though Gate 1 needs a fail-then-what answer.
synthesis_top_issues.cross_exam_summary: adversarial-qa widened it: with systems-designer's death spiral, the reload gives the weakest player the least time and the worst weather, so the save must also cover weather state. business-analyst added that a full restart at minutes 20-30 happens inside Steam's refund window. Four reviewers converged on a run-start or phase-start time snapshot. feasibility-lead disputes BLOCKING for the prototype (Disagreement A).

synthesis_top_issues.title: The fail state can't be shown from where the deadline usually runs out, and the player can't tell why (or even that) they failed
synthesis_top_issues.problem: The deadline can run out mid-crossing, inside the outpost, or on the lighthouse stairs. But the fail is defined as the ship running aground “seen in first person” from the lighthouse, and cutaways are banned. The deadline is also hidden: with one fixed boat speed it works as an invisible count of allowed mistakes, which the ship's lights can't convey. Either way, Pillar 4's promise that the player “always knows ... why they failed” breaks.
synthesis_top_issues.cross_exam_summary: adversarial-qa F1 + player-psychologist F2 turn it into the common case: curious players are most likely to be in the outpost at expiry, with no sightline. feasibility-lead: up to four authored fail presentations vs one budgeted in week 5. systems-designer rejected “let the ship keep going” (unreadable doomed run). Audio-only (horn, then silence) backed by feasibility-lead and systems-designer; narrative-critic accepts it if chosen deliberately.

synthesis_top_issues.title: The passenger ship, the game's only stakes, is never introduced in-game, and the ending it resolves has no human payoff
synthesis_top_issues.problem: No scene tells the player the ship exists or what happens if the beacon stays dark. It first appears as a hidden deadline at boarding. Nobody aboard is named, the aftermath of a fail is undecided, and Ted, Jeff and Daniel never react to either outcome. The whole pressure design (Pillar 2) and the “consequential ending” depend on the player knowing and caring about this ship.
synthesis_top_issues.cross_exam_summary: Two reviewers raised it from MAJOR to BLOCKING. player-psychologist showed four other findings depend on the ship being seen and understood. business-analyst: no pitch line, since a trailer can't sell stakes the game never sets up. The pre-boarding visibility tension was resolved by player-psychologist and narrative-critic both proposing a reveal at the boarding threshold, which adversarial-qa had already listed as acceptable.

synthesis_top_issues.title: Ted is essential to the design, but whether he is physically present is still undecided, and he vanishes after Step 2
synthesis_top_issues.severity_note: Split rating: BLOCKING (narrative-critic) / MAJOR (business-analyst, feasibility-lead, adversarial-qa). Stored severity is the highest assigned; render the split if possible.
synthesis_top_issues.problem: Ted gives the repair guidance, prompts the crash view, orders the gate opened, and explains the errand. He is Pillar 3's answer to “no markers” and the game's only tutorial. Yet “Ted's presence” is listed as an open decision. Even with him confirmed, he has nothing to do in Steps 6-8, and the document never says why an experienced keeper sends a new apprentice into the storm.
synthesis_top_issues.cross_exam_summary: Four reviewers confirmed the diagnosis, but three rejected BLOCKING: one decision the creator can make in a day, blocking only if still open by week 3-4 (Disagreement E). adversarial-qa softened its own Ted point and redirected to Proposed rules already enforced as invariants and gate criteria. narrative-critic's point that Ted has no second-half role stands uncontested.

synthesis_top_issues.title: The hidden clock penalises the wrong players: weather that worsens with elapsed time, a clock running during first steering, and a clock running during outpost exploration
synthesis_top_issues.problem: Collisions cost time, and weather escalates with elapsed time, so struggling players face denser hazards and worse visibility. That is a death spiral. The clock starts at boarding, so a novice's first learning collisions feed straight into it. It also keeps running through the outpost search, where the folk-horror content lives, so the curious player pays twice, in time and in harder weather on the return.
synthesis_top_issues.cross_exam_summary: systems-designer showed three other choices feed the loop (clock during learning, clock during exploration, respawn rules). feasibility-lead: the loop makes tuning from 3-5 week-6 testers unreliable. narrative-critic and business-analyst: the distinctive content sits where the clock punishes engaging with it, so rushing players miss the hook. Weather-driver fix and discovery placement remain disputed (Disagreements B and D).

synthesis_disagreements.question: Is the retry/checkpoint trap BLOCKING for the prototype, or only for Gate 2?
synthesis_disagreements.side_a_position: BLOCKING now. The Gate 1 slice has to reach both outcomes, and a Gate 1 acceptance criterion that depends on a Gate 3 system means the prototype can't pass its own gate (adversarial-qa). Playtesters can't judge fairness with no retry model (systems-designer).
synthesis_disagreements.side_b_position: MAJOR for the prototype, BLOCKING for Gate 2. “Fail, then restart the slice” is a valid, nearly free Gate 1 answer for a 10-minute build. The trap only becomes real once checkpoints exist.
synthesis_disagreements.other_positions: Common ground: all agree on the snapshot fix.
synthesis_disagreements.escalated_decision: Does Gate 1 accept “restart the slice” as its retry model, or must the final retry and save model be settled before the prototype is built?

synthesis_disagreements.question: What should drive storm escalation?
synthesis_disagreements.side_a_position: Escalate by phase and route position only, or cap the share driven by elapsed time. Otherwise the loop punishes struggling players twice and can't be tuned offline. (systems-designer, backed by feasibility-lead and player-psychologist)
synthesis_disagreements.side_b_position: Tying weather only to position breaks Pillar 2 (“The storm sets the clock”): struggling and skilled players would see the same sky at the same rock, and the world would stop reporting lateness. Split the channel: the readable storm (sound, lightning, wind, ship lights) follows elapsed time, and hazard density follows phase and position.
synthesis_disagreements.escalated_decision: Does elapsed time drive anything the player collides with, or only what the player perceives?

synthesis_disagreements.question: Should the return crossing branch into a riskier shortcut?
synthesis_disagreements.side_a_position: Yes. It gives the pressure an outlet without a second control, gives repairs a mechanical output, uses the dead “unlocked routes” field, and adds replay value. systems-designer rates it MAJOR in combination.
synthesis_disagreements.side_b_position: feasibility-lead: no branching in the prototype; the hazard forecast is built around one safe-route signal and week 4 is already overloaded; cheaper to cut the unused save field. adversarial-qa: at fixed speed a survivable shortcut is always optimal; it breaks the singular safe-route signal behind Jeff's calls and doubles the tuning load.
synthesis_disagreements.other_positions: business-analyst: defer to Gate 2 and put it on the ranked cut list.
synthesis_disagreements.escalated_decision: Commit to route choice, which means designing the forecast API for multiple routes from day one, or remove “unlocked routes” from the save contract?

synthesis_disagreements.question: Where should the optional folk-horror discoveries live?
synthesis_disagreements.side_a_position: Move them before boarding, to the lighthouse and island. That removes the time penalty on the game's distinctive content, keeps prototype tuning data valid (the outpost won't grow after week 6), and reuses environments that already have to be built. narrative-critic partly agrees: the core of the wrongness can live in the lighthouse if tied to why the beacon failed.
synthesis_disagreements.side_b_position: Citing systems-designer F4 (and having withdrawn the move-pre-boarding fix in Round 2): moving more untimed content into a front half that already holds about 20 of the 30 minutes worsens the pacing imbalance. Keep discoveries at the outpost, budget explicit exploration time, and have Jeff signal when it's used up.
synthesis_disagreements.other_positions: narrative-critic partly agrees with side A.
synthesis_disagreements.escalated_decision: Protect the atmosphere by moving discoveries into the untimed act, or protect pacing by keeping them in the timed act with a budgeted allowance?

synthesis_disagreements.question: How severe is Ted's open status, and should he return in the second half?
synthesis_disagreements.side_a_position: BLOCKING. Beyond the open decision, Ted has no arc after Step 2. He should be at the lamp for the climax and react to both outcomes.
synthesis_disagreements.side_b_position: MAJOR with a “needed by” date (week 3 per feasibility-lead, before week 4 per business-analyst). feasibility-lead warns every added Ted beat is unpriced voice-over cost and would allow only lines delivered from the lighthouse (radio or window). business-analyst proposes spending the ending's human payoff on Ted and folding Daniel into Jeff.
synthesis_disagreements.escalated_decision: Lock Ted's presence by a fixed week, and decide whether his second-half role is a staged scene or voice-only lines.

synthesis_quick_wins.title: Replace “save remaining time at checkpoints” with a run-start or phase-start time snapshot
synthesis_quick_wins.description: Reword the invariant to “resolves exactly once per attempt.” This removes the doomed-save loop with no floor logic.

synthesis_quick_wins.title: Start the deadline when the player clears the harbour mouth, not on boarding
synthesis_quick_wins.description: One trigger volume that gives a free steering warm-up and removes the earliest input to the death spiral. (player-psychologist F3; feasibility-lead and business-analyst specified this near-zero-cost version)

synthesis_quick_wins.title: Script the ship reveal at the boarding threshold
synthesis_quick_wins.description: Ted names the ship's lights as the reason for the errand. This introduces the stakes, starts the clock on a story beat, and removes the frozen-ship window. (compatible with adversarial-qa F5)

synthesis_verdict.verdict_one_line: This document is not ready to drive full production, and its prototype is not ready to test fairly until the fail loop is defined.
synthesis_verdict.single_most_important_change: Write the fail-state contract before week 5: what the player perceives when the deadline expires in each phase, how the world tells them why, and what a retry restores (a run-start or phase-start snapshot). Issues #1, #2 and #3 all depend on that one decision.
synthesis_verdict.full_paragraph: This document is not ready to drive full production, and its prototype is not ready to test fairly until the fail loop is defined. The board found the prototype plan unusually disciplined (feasibility-lead): a hard Gate 0 go/no-go, waves isolated behind a toggle, and a clean state contract. But the only failure system in the game has no decided retry model, no way to be shown where it usually triggers, no way for the player to read why it happened, and no introduced stakes for it to resolve. Five of six reviewers independently landed on some part of that loop. Beyond the prototype, feasibility-lead and business-analyst agree that "the full game's feasibility cannot be judged from this document as written," because there is no schedule, estimate or cut list past week 6. The single change that matters most is to write the fail-state contract before week 5: what the player perceives when the deadline expires in each phase, how the world tells them why, and what a retry restores (a run-start or phase-start snapshot). Issues #1, #2 and #3 all depend on that one decision.
